findings.detail: The denoising implementation follows the train-only symmetrized, degree-corrected neighbor averaging and normalization in lines 202-230, but this runner hardcodes only lambda=0.1. The stated protocol requires comparing lambda in {0.1, 0.3, 0.5} and selecting solely by the predeclared validation protocol; the comment says selection is downstream, but this entry point neither produces those candidates nor implements selection.
findings.reproduction: Run this entry point as configured: every embedding passed to RQVAE is denoised with strength 0.1 (line 296); no run in this code path tests the other two specified strengths or validation-based selection.
findings.correction: Make the candidate strength an explicit run configuration and provide the three specified candidate runs, with selection restricted to the predeclared validation procedure; keep all graph construction train-only.

findings.detail: The distributed trainer deadlocks at codebook initialization. Only rank 0 calls init_codebook, but VQLayer.init_codebook unconditionally executes distributed.broadcast when a process group is initialized (model/layers.py:139-144). The other ranks skip this call and reach the barrier at line 350, so rank 0 waits in broadcast while the peers wait in barrier. This prevents the real four-rank launcher from completing training or exporting SIDs.
findings.reproduction: Invoke the normal top-level entry point with its configured torchrun 4-rank launcher and available inputs: rank 0 enters raw_module.init_codebook at line 348 and blocks in broadcast; ranks 1-3 proceed to dist.barrier at line 350. The run cannot advance to the first epoch.
findings.correction: Have every rank participate in the same codebook initialization collectives (with the same ordered calls), or initialize on rank 0 and explicitly broadcast the resulting codebook state using matching collectives on all ranks. Then keep the barrier only after all ranks have completed that shared initialization.
